rpact - Confirmatory Adaptive Clinical Trial Design and Analysis

Source: R/pkgname.R
rpact.Rd

rpact (R Package for Adaptive Clinical Trials) supports the design, simulation, and analysis of confirmatory clinical trials. It provides sample size and power calculations for standard fixed-sample and classical group sequential designs, with methods for continuous, binary, survival (time-to-event), and count data endpoints. Adaptive methods include multi-stage combination tests, sample size reassessment, multi-arm multi-stage (MAMS) designs, and population enrichment designs. The package implements a broad range of methods described by Wassmer and Brannath (2025).

Details

Planning and simulation functions are available for means, rates, survival, and count data. Survival planning supports staggered recruitment and piecewise exponentially distributed survival times. Multi-arm and population enrichment simulation and analysis methods are available for means, rates, and survival endpoints. General estimates and standard errors can also be analyzed through getDataset() and getAnalysisResults().

Classical group sequential designs specify rules for interim and final analyses. Alpha-spending approaches allow boundary recalculation for observed information, including under- and over-running. Adaptations based on interim treatment effects require methods that preserve Type I error control, such as combination testing or the conditional rejection probability (CRP) principle. The package provides inverse normal and Fisher combination tests and conditional Dunnett methods. Simulations can assess the operating characteristics of sample size or event-number reassessment strategies.

Analysis methods provide p-values, conditional power, and confidence intervals where supported by the selected design and endpoint. In particular, final confidence intervals and median unbiased estimates are not available for Fisher combination tests or multi-arm and enrichment analyses. See getAnalysisResults() for further conditions and limitations. getFutilityBounds() converts futility boundaries between different scales, including conditional and predictive power scales.

rpact is free of charge and open source under the LGPL-3 license. Package information and tutorials are available at www.rpact.org; function documentation is available at docs.rpact.org.

RPACT GmbH develops Statistical Tools for Drug Development and offers software development, validation, technical support, consulting, and training. Formal validation documentation is available to customers and supporting members. It includes credentials for the full installation qualification test suite run by testPackage(). For services, see www.rpact.com. Browser-based tools are available at demo.rpact.cloud (RPACT Cloud) and connect.rpact.app (RPACT Connect).
